A lantern, a radio, a switch. With the same command to turn on and off (for example "use") it creates 2 rules that alternate; with two different commands it creates 4, with the answers "already on / off".
Afterwards, describe the room again (useful for lights)

A box, a trunk, a drawer: the contents can be seen and taken only when it is open. Marks the object as a container that opens and closes and creates the rules to open it (2) and, if you like, to close it again (2 more). When it opens, the game says by itself what is inside. For a locked container use "Open or unlock with another object" instead.

The character answers differently the first time, the second, and from the third on. Creates 3 rules (or 2 if you leave the second answer empty) and a variable that counts the times. If missing, it adds the new command.

ask about the house, "talk to anna about the key": the character answers about a topic, something you can talk about even if it is not there. Creates the topic (if new) and a rule: it answers if the character is in the room, otherwise it says the fallback sentence. With several characters in the room, the one chosen here answers.

A guard in front of a door, someone barring the path: the exit can be used only after the character has stepped aside, which happens when the player does the chosen action (giving it an object, showing it something, talking to it). Creates a rule, adds to the exit the condition "the character has stepped aside" and gives the character a description for when it has moved (its "open" variant). A shortcut for the most common situations: choose the type, fill in a few fields and the app creates the complete rules. New rules go to the bottom of the list and are edited like the others; if there are already rules for the same sentence (for example "talk gardener"), the new ones go right before them, so they really fire.
close (new command, added to the words)
To delete it, first remove the conditions and actions that use it.

A variable is a number from 0 to 255 that the game remembers: for example attempts made, points or how many times you have talked to someone. It is tested in the rules' conditions and changed with the actions "Set", "Increase" and "Decrease". A small maximum keeps the solution check fast.
They must all be true. If there are none, the event always fires.

Rules make things happen when the player types a command. The first matching rule applies: if its conditions are not true and there is an "otherwise", it stops there; if not, it moves on to the next rule. If no rule acts, the command does what it would do by default.

An event fires when the player enters a room (or at the start of the game, if it starts there), after the description. All the matching ones fire, in order. "Only the first time" is for scenes and encounters. If the event must never repeat under other conditions, use a variable.
